title: How to Help Prevent Ingrown Hairs After a Brazilian Wax
summary: Learn the 7 steps you can take to help prevent ingrown hairs in your bikini area, plus how to spot the difference between ingrown hairs and folliculitis.
body_markdown:
The whole point of getting a Brazilian wax? To enjoy weeks of smooth skin afterward.


So


when ingrown hairs show up and get in the way of your results, it can feel frustrating.


While some people are more prone to ingrown


hairs


than others,


they're


not entirely out of your control. A few simple changes to your skincare routine and waxing habits can make


a big difference


.


Whether


you're


preparing for your first


Brazilian, or


trying to get rid of stubborn


ingrowns


after your latest wax,


here's


how to keep bumps to a minimum.


## Is it Normal to Get Ingrown Hairs After a Brazilian Wax?


Yes, it can be normal to experience some ingrown hairs after a Brazilian wax. While ingrown hairs can happen anywhere, the bikini area is especially prone to them for three reasons:


-


The skin in the bikini area is sensitive.


-


Pubic hair is often coarser and curlier than hair on other parts of the body.


-


The bikini area is naturally prone to friction from everyday movement and clothing.


That said, dealing with lots of ingrown


hairs


after every wax


isn't


something you should have to accept as part of your routine. Luckily, there are ways to


help


reduce the risk of getting them.


An ingrown


hair develops when hair grows back into the skin instead of outward. This can cause raised bumps that may become red, itchy, or irritated.


Want


to understand more? Read our


[complete guide to what causes ingrown hairs](https://waxcenter.com/blogs/news/so-what-causes-ingrown-hairs?utm_source=chatgpt.com) .


## What's


the Difference Between


an Ingrown


Hair and F


olliculitis


?


Ingrown hairs and


[folliculitis](https://waxcenter.com/blogs/news/preventing-and-treating-folliculitis-after-waxing) can look similar, but


they're


not the same thing.


An ingrown


hair occurs when hair grows back into the skin instead of out, while folliculitis is a generalized term that means inflammation around a hair follicle.


**Ingrown hair**


**Folliculitis**


Caused by hair growing into the skin


Caused by inflammation of the hair follicle


Often appears as an isolated bump, sometimes with a trapped hair visible


May appear as clusters of pimple-like bumps


Typically develops as hair starts growing back after waxing


May appear


immediately


or within the first few days after waxing


Both can occur after waxing, and their symptoms sometimes overlap, which can be confusing. That said, there are a few telltale signs to look for.


Ingrown hairs often appear as individual, sometimes larger bumps, and you may be able to see


a hair


trapped beneath the skin. Folliculitis is more likely to show up as clusters of smaller, red, pimple-like bumps. Timing can also be a clue: folliculitis typically develops shortly after waxing, while ingrown hairs usually appear later as hair starts growing back.


## How to Help Prevent Ingrown Hairs After a Brazilian Wax


The three most important things you can do to help prevent ingrown hairs after a Brazilian wax are avoiding heat and friction while your skin recovers, exfoliating every 2–3 days, and moisturizing daily.


You can further reduce your risk by using a specialty serum, avoiding shaving between appointments, and sticking to a consistent


[waxing schedule](https://waxcenter.com/blogs/news/how-often-should-you-wax-each-body-area-a-head-to-toe-schedule) .


Here's


a breakdown of everything that helps minimize the risk of ingrown hairs between


waxes


.


### 1. Wear


Loose


Clothing to Your Appointment


What you wear to your Brazilian wax matters. Tight clothing can rub against freshly waxed skin, causing irritation that may contribute to ingrown


hairs


. Show up in something loose and


comfortable, and


give your skin room to breathe afterward.


What clothing makes ingrown


hairs


worse?


Tight leggings, skinny jeans, restrictive underwear, and sweaty workout clothes can increase friction and trap heat and moisture against your bikini area. Stick to loose-fitting clothes and, if possible, breathable cotton underwear.


### 2. Follow Proper Brazilian Wax Aftercare


After a Brazilian wax, your skin needs


[the right aftercare](https://waxcenter.com/pages/brazilian-waxing-aftercare) to recover. For the first 24–


48 hours


, avoid anything that could cause extra irritation, including:


-


Hot baths, saunas, and steam rooms.


-


Intense workouts and excessive sweating.


-


Harsh scrubs, exfoliating acids, and


fragranced


skincare.


-


Tight clothing that rubs against your bikini area.


Some temporary redness or sensitivity is normal. Give your skin time to settle before returning to your regular skincare routine.


### 3. Exfoliate Regularly to Prevent Trapped Hairs


Exfoliating your bikini area every 2-3 days is one of the best ways to help prevent ingrown hairs after a Brazilian wax. Dead skin cells can trap new growth beneath the surface, forcing them to grow back inward.


[Regular exfoliation](https://waxcenter.com/blogs/news/exfoliation-explained) helps clear the way for hair to grow as it should.


There are two main ways to exfoliate:


-


Physical exfoliation:


Manually removes dead skin cells with a body polish or soft washcloth.


-


Chemical exfoliation:


Uses ingredients like salicylic or glycolic acid to loosen dead skin cells.


For


maximum


efficacy, look for a product like the


[EWC TREAT® Get Smooth Skin Clearing Body Polish](https://waxcenter.com/products/get-smooth-skin-clearing-body-polish) , which combines the benefits of both physical and chemical exfoliation.


How soon after a Brazilian wax should you start exfoliating?


Wait at least


48 hours


after your Brazilian wax before exfoliating, and make sure any redness and sensitivity have subsided. Then, gently exfoliate every 2–3 days, depending on your skin's tolerance.


### 4. Use an Ingrown Hair Serum


If


you’re


especially prone to


ingrowns


after a Brazilian wax,


[using an ingrown hair serum](https://waxcenter.com/blogs/news/how-do-serums-for-ingrown-hairs-work) can help prevent


the appearance of


bumps and keep follicles clear.


Our


[EWC TREAT® Ingrown Hair Serum](https://waxcenter.com/products/ingrown-hair-serum-ewc) is a guest favorite for a reason.


It’s


formulated to help treat and prevent


the appearance of


ingrown hairs and is safe to use


on


the bikini area


.


### 5. Moisturize Your Bikini Area Daily


Exfoliation and hydration go hand in hand. Moisturizing helps prevent dryness and supports your skin's natural barrier as new hair grows, which also makes future waxes easier and more effective.


Apply a


[moisturizer for your skin type](https://waxcenter.com/collections/all?filter.p.product_type=Moisturizers&filter.v.price.gte=&filter.v.price.lte=&sort_by=manual) to clean, dry skin daily.


### 6. Wax Consistently Without Shaving In-Between


Sticking to a consistent Brazilian waxing schedule, typically every 3–4 weeks, can help reduce


ingrowns


. Over time, regrowth may become softer and finer, while a regular schedule helps keep hair growth cycles more aligned, allowing for more thorough hair removal with each wax.


Tempted to reach for your razor between appointments?


Resist


the urge. Shaving disrupts the hair growth cycle and cuts hair at the surface, leaving sharp tips that can curl back into the skin and become ingrown.


### 7. Leave Hair Removal to the Experts


Proper hair removal technique is key to helping prevent ingrown hairs. When hair breaks instead of being removed from the root, it can increase the likelihood of


ingrowns


.

## How to Help Get Rid of Ingrown


Pubic


Hairs After a Brazilian Wax


If you develop an ingrown hair after a Brazilian wax, a warm compress, gentle exfoliation, and proper skincare can help release the trapped hair. Most importantly, resist the urge to squeeze or dig it out, which can make irritation worse.


Here's


what to do instead:


1.


Apply a warm compress.


Gently press a warm, damp washcloth against the bump for 5–10 minutes to help soften the skin.


1.


Gently exfoliate.


If the skin isn't irritated, use a soft washcloth or


[EWC TREAT® Brightening Ingrown Hair Wipes](https://waxcenter.com/products/brightening-ingrown-hair-wipes) to help remove dead skin cells.


1.


Leave trapped


hairs


alone.


If the hair


doesn't release


on its own,


don't


dig or squeeze. Instead, gently repeat this process for a few days.


1.


Cleanse and moisturize.


Keep the area clean and hydrated.


For more tips, check out our


[complete guide to ingrown hair self-care](https://waxcenter.com/blogs/news/a-complete-guide-to-ingrown-hair-self-care) .


## Is it okay to pull out an ingrown pubic hair?


If an ingrown hair is still trapped beneath the skin,


don't


try to dig it out with tweezers or your fingernails. This can cause further irritation or scarring. If the hair has fully


emerged


, it is


generally safe


to remove it gently with clean tweezers.


If an ingrown hair is particularly painful, keeps coming back, or


doesn't


improve, consult a dermatologist or healthcare provider.
